Available on the Pro and Founder plans and during an active trial. On the Free plan, or after a trial ends, the toggle is disabled and shows a Pro badge that links to Settings > Plan. A saved Turbo Mode setting is treated as off on those plans. Claude Code CLI​ Installation status: Shows if the CLI is detected Installation command: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code Sonar API Key​ Configure a SonarCloud or SonarQube API key that is automatically injected into agent terminal sessions as the SONAR_API_KEY environment variable. The key is for SonarCloud code quality and static analysis, not AI-powered search. Setting Up Go to Settings Scroll to the Sonar API Key section Enter your Sonar API key Click Save -- the key is stored securely via Electron safeStorage How It Works When a task execution starts, CrewDeck retrieves the key and injects it into the PTY environment Agents and MCP tools that interact with SonarCloud/SonarQube can authenticate automatically The key is never written to disk in plaintext -- it exists only in the PTY process environment at runtime If no key is configured, the environment variable is simply omitted Secrets and MCP Server Credentials​ Settings › AI & Tools has a Secrets card directly above MCP Servers. Secrets comes first because a secret must exist before you can attach it to a server. To store an API key for an MCP server such as New Relic and attach it as an environment variable or HTTP header, see Custom Secrets for MCP Servers. Cloud Sync Passkeys​ Setting up CloudSync (Settings › CloudSync) is passwordless and takes two rounds before you choose your encryption passphrase: Email code -- enter the code sent to your email address Passkey -- register a passkey (the first time) or use the one already on your account The passkey prompt When you click Register passkey or Continue with passkey, CrewDeck opens your browser to show the passkey prompt. You can use: this device's built-in authenticator (for example Touch ID) a phone, by scanning the QR code the prompt shows a security key If the passkey step doesn't finish CrewDeck shows a message inside the passkey step explaining what happened. Each one offers a way forward. Message What it means Retry? Passkey cancelled The prompt was closed before it finished Yes Passkey timed out The prompt wasn't completed in time Yes Passkeys aren't supported here This browser or device can't use a passkey -- try again with a phone or a security key Yes Couldn't open the passkey prompt CrewDeck couldn't open your browser Yes Passkey not accepted The passkey step was cancelled or failed on the server Yes Passkey result didn't arrive The result from your browser never reached CrewDeck Yes A passkey prompt is already open Finish or close the open prompt first Yes Passkey already registered This authenticator already holds a passkey for this account -- sign in with it instead No No passkey on this account The account has no passkey yet, so it can't be unlocked on this device No Retry is safe: cancelling or timing out does not use up an attempt. When Retry isn't offered, running the same prompt again would fail the same way. Not now vs. Start over Not now (while registering a new passkey) cancels setup. Nothing is saved, CloudSync stays off, and the next time you set it up you'll be asked for a passkey again. Start over (while using an existing passkey) cancels this sign-in and returns you to the email step with your email address kept. A passkey is required. There is no SMS or password-only alternative, and no way to finish setup without one. Setup unavailable If the CloudSync tab shows a disabled Set up Cloud Sync button, this installation has no passkey page configured. Setup turns on automatically once it is. Remote Database​ Remote database keeps a status copy of your work in the cloud so CrewDeck Web can show your board and your history while this Mac is asleep. The section lives in Settings › CloudSync, below the CloudSync panel where you sign in to your account. It is off until you turn it on, and it needs CloudSync switched on with an account linked on this Mac. Each field in that copy is either readable by the server -- so it can sort, filter, page and count -- or encrypted with your CloudSync key, which the server never holds. What the server can read Across your full history of projects, epics, tasks, releases, repos and agents: Task IDs, statuses and stages Priorities and sizes Dates: when items were created, started, updated, completed, published and released Which project, epic or repo each item belongs to Which agents each task is assigned to Release IDs, statuses and pull request numbers Dependency links between tasks and release links to tasks Ciphertext lengths of the encrypted fields What stays encrypted Uploaded only as ciphertext, task descriptions included: Project, epic, repo and agent names Task titles and task numbers Task descriptions Release versions, titles and notes Three things worth knowing It covers your full history, not a recent window. There is no 30-day limit: every task you have ever run is included, apart from workflow-run tasks. How much history fits is governed by your cloud storage quota. Task descriptions are uploaded, encrypted. Each one is capped at 8 KiB in the cloud copy; when you open a task in the browser, the full text is read live from this Mac, which therefore has to be awake. Execution data is never stored in the cloud. Terminal output, run transcripts, command-step output and diffs are read live from this Mac, end-to-end encrypted on the way, and are never kept on the server. In short: an operator with access to the Remote database can see the shape and cadence of every task you have ever run -- counts, statuses, priorities, sizes, timing, dependency graph, release membership and ciphertext lengths -- though never titles, names, descriptions or notes. Remote Access​ Remote access lets the CrewDeck iPhone app reach this Mac from any network, through a relay. Requests are end-to-end encrypted, so the relay only ever holds ciphertext. The section lives in Settings › CloudSync, below the CloudSync panel where you sign in to your account. Turning it on Go to Settings and open the CloudSync tab Scroll to Remote access, below the CloudSync panel Sign in to your CrewDeck account in the CloudSync panel above if you have not already. This is the only prerequisite: CloudSync does not need to be set up or unlocked Flip the Remote access toggle on Remote access is off by default, and only one Mac per account can hold it at a time. Turning it on here takes the account over from any other Mac that had it on. Reading the status strip State What it means Connected to relay This Mac is reachable from your phone Connecting... The relay connection is being established or retried Disconnected The relay is unreachable; the strip names the reason (signed out, not configured in this build, taken over by another Mac, or a connection error) Next to the state, Last snapshot shows when CrewDeck last sent your phone a fresh view of projects and tasks. It reads "No snapshot published yet" until the first one goes out, which happens shortly after the relay connects and a phone is paired. Pairing a phone With Remote access on, click Pair a phone Scan the QR code with the CrewDeck iPhone app, or type the six-character code shown under it The four steps tick off as the phone connects; the device is then added below with full access The code expires after a few minutes. Click Show a new code to start over. Local network (Wi-Fi) The Local network (Wi-Fi) subsection is a separate transport with its own toggle. It starts a local HTTP server so a phone on the same Wi-Fi can pair without the relay, and it is unaffected by the Remote access toggle. Configure its port there and use Generate Pairing QR Code to pair. Paired devices Every paired device is listed with how it reached this Mac ("Paired over the relay" or "Paired on Wi-Fi"), when it paired and when it was last seen. Change a device between Full access and Read-only, or Revoke it to cut it off entirely. Revoked devices are removed from the list. Anonymous Usage Telemetry​ CrewDeck includes an opt-in anonymous telemetry system to help improve the application. Telemetry is disabled by default and all data is stored locally on your device. Enabling Telemetry Go to Settings Scroll to the Telemetry section Toggle Enable telemetry to turn it on Granular Category Controls You can enable or disable specific telemetry categories independently: Category What Is Tracked Feature Usage Which features are used (not content or data) Workflow Metrics Task completion rates UI Engagement Page views and interactions Performance App startup time and operation durations Data Management Action Description Export Download all telemetry data as a JSON file for review Clear Delete all collected telemetry data (with confirmation prompt) Privacy Guarantees No data leaves your device without an explicit export action, or the separate opt-in Grafana Cloud export described under Data & Privacy No personally identifiable information (PII) is collected Timestamps are rounded to hour precision to prevent event correlation Metadata keys that might contain PII (email, username, path, etc.) are automatically rejected Events older than 90 days are automatically deleted Maximum 10,000 events stored First-Run Opt-In Prompt On first launch, CrewDeck displays a one-time dialog asking whether you want to enable analytics. The dialog explains clearly what is collected, how identifiers are anonymized, and presents equally weighted "Enable Analytics" and "No Thanks" buttons. Your choice is saved immediately — the dialog never reappears. You can change your preference at any time in Settings > Telemetry. Grafana Cloud Export​ Separately from local telemetry storage, CrewDeck can export traces, metrics and logs to the team's Grafana Cloud OTLP endpoint. This is off by default and requires explicit opt-in. Enabling Export Go to Settings > Data & Privacy Toggle Share diagnostics with Grafana Cloud to turn it on Export only happens when all of the following are true: Anonymous Usage Telemetry is enabled, the Grafana Cloud toggle is on, and an access token is stored on this device. Turning off either switch stops export immediately — no data is sent to Grafana Cloud otherwise. A health readout below the toggle reports the current export status. In-App Feedback​ CrewDeck can prompt you for satisfaction feedback after completing key workflows. This helps identify which features work well and which need improvement. Feedback Prompts When enabled, feedback prompts appear after: Workflow When Prompted Task completion When a task is moved to "Done" status Release creation After a successful release is created Debate completion When a multi-agent debate concludes Agent installation After installing an agent from the marketplace Providing Feedback A feedback widget appears with 1-5 star rating Select a rating (labels: Poor, Fair, Good, Very Good, Excellent) Optionally add a comment (up to 500 characters) Click Submit to save, or Skip to dismiss Configuring Feedback Go to Settings Scroll to the Feedback section Use the master toggle to enable or disable all feedback prompts Use per-category toggles to control which workflows prompt for feedback Click View Feedback to browse all stored feedback entries Click Clear to delete all feedback data (with confirmation) Privacy All feedback data is stored locally in the SQLite database Maximum 1,000 feedback records are retained (oldest records auto-deleted) Records older than 365 days are automatically cleaned up Feedback data can be included in telemetry exports Plan and Billing​ The Plan tab shows your current plan and lets you choose one. Plan picker: Pro is $10 per month or $96 per year. Founder is a one-time $149 lifetime purchase. Paddle takes payment and handles tax. Manage billing: Shown for accounts that purchased through Paddle. It opens Paddle's customer portal in your browser, where you can cancel, update the card on file and download invoices. If no billing record exists for your account, it shows "Billing management isn't available for this account yet." Legal links: The picker footer links to the Terms of Service, Privacy Policy and Refund Policy. Each opens in your browser.

The Security Dashboard provides a unified view of security-relevant events recorded by CrewDeck's SQLite event store. It surfaces audit data from command approvals, agent permission checks, IPC validation failures, and terminal session activity. Accessing the Security Dashboard Click Settings in the sidebar Navigate to the Security tab The Security Dashboard loads the most recent 500 security events Event Categories Category Events Tracked Command Approvals All command approval decisions (approved, rejected, timed out) with command strings and risk classifications IPC Validation Requests that failed Zod schema validation on task execution channels Permission Checks Agent capability enforcement decisions — which operations were permitted or blocked Session Lifecycle Terminal session start, stop, kill, and crash events Sandbox Violations Renderer-side attempts to access Node.js APIs outside the context bridge Filtering and Search Use the filter bar at the top of the Security Dashboard to: Filter by event category Filter by severity (info, warning, error) Search by task ID, session ID, or agent name Set a date range (default: last 7 days) Event Detail View Click any event row to expand the full event payload, which includes: Timestamp (millisecond precision) Event category and severity Entity references (task ID, session ID, agent name) Raw event payload (JSON) Export Click Export Events to download filtered security events as a JSON file for external audit tools or incident investigation. Retention Security events follow the same 90-day retention policy as other state events. The maximum stored event count is shared with the global event sourcing limit (1 million events). Security events are prioritized during cleanup; other event categories are pruned first when the limit is approached. Why This Matters The Security Dashboard gives teams visibility into: Which commands agents are running and whether any required approval Whether agents are operating within their declared capability boundaries IPC anomalies that may indicate unexpected renderer behavior A complete audit trail for compliance and incident response

CrewDeck writes a sandbox block into Claude Code's .claude/settings.local.json file when a task begins execution. This block restricts what Claude Code can access on the filesystem, which network domains it may reach, and whether it can run commands outside the sandbox. Accessing Sandbox Settings Click Settings in the sidebar Navigate to the Security tab Scroll to the Terminal Sandbox section Configurable Policy Fields Setting Default Description Denied Directories /etc, /var, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws Filesystem paths Claude Code cannot read or write Allowed Directories (empty) Additional filesystem paths Claude Code may access beyond the worktree. The worktree path is always auto-included. Tilde (~) paths are expanded at write time. Allowed Domains (empty) Network domains Claude Code may contact during execution Unix Sockets ~/.ssh/agent-socket Unix socket paths Claude Code may connect to (e.g., for SSH agent operations) Allow Unsandboxed Commands Off When enabled, allows Claude Code to run commands outside the sandbox constraints How It Works When a task execution begins, CrewDeck writes the following structure into the worktree's .claude/settings.local.json: { "permissions": { "...existing..." }, "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "allowedDirectories": ["/path/to/worktree", "/additional/path"], "deniedDirectories": ["/etc", "/var", "~/.ssh", "~/.aws"], "allowedDomains": [], "network": { "allowUnixSockets": ["~/.ssh/agent-socket"] }, "allowUnsandboxedCommands": false } } The worktree directory is always the first entry in allowedDirectories and is auto-included regardless of user configuration. Any additional paths added in the Allowed Directories setting are merged and deduplicated. Tilde (~) paths are expanded to the user's home directory at write time. When Execution Completes The sandbox block is removed from .claude/settings.local.json when the worktree is cleaned up, leaving the file in its original state. Updating Sandbox Policy Open the Sandbox Settings panel in Settings > Security > Terminal Sandbox Modify the desired fields: Type a path or domain and click Deny / Allow to add it to the relevant list Click the remove button next to an existing entry to delete it Toggle Allow Unsandboxed Commands on or off Click Save Policy The new policy takes effect on the next task execution

Some MCP servers have their own CrewDeck setup flow. For example, connecting GitHub provisions GH_TOKEN for the GitHub MCP server. For every other server, such as New Relic, store the API key once as a secret and attach it to the server. Do not paste the key into the server's Headers or Config fields. Creating a Secret​ Go to Settings › AI & Tools › Secrets and click Add Secret Key: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit, up to 128 characters (for example NEW_RELIC_API_KEY) Value: up to 8,192 characters. The value must not contain a ${NAME} placeholder Description (optional): a note to help you recognise the secret later Click Add Secret Rules The value is encrypted on this device and is never shown again. The list shows a fixed •••••••• mask that says nothing about the value's length or content To edit a secret, click Edit on its row. Leave Value blank to keep the stored value, or enter a new value to replace it, then click Save Changes Keys must be unique Names that CrewDeck provisions itself are reserved and rejected: GH_TOKEN, SONAR_API_KEY, CODACY_ACCOUNT_TOKEN, CREWDECK_BASE_BRANCH, CREWDECK_STOP_HOOK_DIR, CREWDECK_NOTIFICATION_HOOK_DIR and CREWDECK_GIT_GUARD_DIR Names that change how a program is found or loaded are rejected: PATH, NODE_OPTIONS, HOME, SHELL, LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH and any name starting with DYLD_ Attaching a Secret to an MCP Server (New Relic example)​ In Settings › AI & Tools › MCP Servers, add the server with Server Type http and the MCP endpoint URL from New Relic's documentation, then save it. Secrets can only be attached to a saved server, so click Edit on the server to reopen it In the server's Secrets area, click Attach Secret Choose your secret from Select a secret Enter the target name: For an http server this is the Header name your provider documents. The field suggests Api-Key; use whatever header name New Relic's documentation gives For a stdio server this is the Env var name the server reads, for example NEW_RELIC_API_KEY Click Save Secrets Notes A server can carry at most 32 attached secrets The server must be enabled for the project the task runs in. Secrets attached to a server that is not enabled for the project are not passed to that run If your provider needs a prefix, such as Authorization: Bearer <token>, type the header yourself in the server's Headers field as Authorization: Bearer ${NEW_RELIC_API_KEY}. CrewDeck keeps a reference you wrote rather than overwriting it If the target name already holds a literal value, the attachment replaces that value with the reference Host and Content-Length cannot be used as header names Changing the Server Type between stdio and http invalidates existing attachments, because an env var only applies to stdio and a header only applies to http. A mismatched attachment is flagged and skipped at launch. Save the type change, reopen the server, correct the attachment's target name and click Save Secrets The resulting entry in the worktree's .mcp.json holds only the reference, never the value: { "mcpServers": { "new-relic": { "type": "http", "url": "https://<your-new-relic-mcp-endpoint>", "headers": { "Api-Key": "${NEW_RELIC_API_KEY}" } } } } How ${VAR} References Are Resolved​ When a task runs, CrewDeck writes each server entry into the worktree's .mcp.json (and .codex/config.toml for Codex) with ${KEY} references only For the servers in that run, CrewDeck decrypts each attached value and places it in the agent run's environment The tool that launches the MCP server replaces each ${KEY} with the matching value from that environment Only CrewDeck's own run environment is used to resolve a reference. Other variables from your shell are never consulted, so an unrelated environment variable cannot be pulled into a server's config A reference that does not match an attached secret is left exactly as written, and the server reports a missing variable or fails to authenticate. A typo in a target name therefore shows up as an authentication failure, not as an error in Settings If the operating system's credential store is unavailable or a value cannot be decrypted, that attachment is skipped with a warning and the run continues without it Values are read again on every run. Nothing is cached between runs beyond the credential store's short-lived cache Why Values Never Appear in Committed Config​ .mcp.json and .codex/config.toml only ever contain ${KEY} references, so committing or sharing them exposes no credential The resolved value lives only in the agent run's environment and in the worktree's local .claude/settings.local.json. CrewDeck adds that file to the worktree's .gitignore, and when CrewDeck commits a run's work it also unstages it, together with .mcp.json and .codex/config.toml, so it does not end up in a commit or pull request. This is the same handling GH_TOKEN already gets The value never comes back to the UI. Settings only ever receives the fixed mask CrewDeck's own log and warning messages name the key or server, never the value Terminal output masks a secret's literal value when it is between 8 and 512 characters long. Shorter or longer values are still passed to the server but are not masked in terminal output Deleting or Rotating a Secret​ To delete a secret, click Delete on its row, then Confirm. The confirmation lists the servers that will lose the credential on their next run. Deleting removes the secret from every server it was attached to Sessions that are already running keep the old value until they are restarted. If a key has leaked, also rotate it at the provider Replacing a value, or attaching a secret to a server, takes effect on the next run GitHub Token (GH_TOKEN) Setup Is Unchanged​ Connecting GitHub (Device Flow or Personal Access Token in Settings › Integrations) still provisions GH_TOKEN for the GitHub MCP server exactly as before. Custom secrets cannot use GH_TOKEN or any other CrewDeck-provisioned name, cannot override it, and do not change the GitHub server's generated config. Existing GitHub setups need no action.

Cause: GitHub is not authenticated. Solution: Go to Settings Use Device Flow (recommended): click Sign in with GitHub, then visit github.com/login/device and enter the displayed code Alternatively, enter your GitHub Personal Access Token and click Connect GitHub Ensure the token has the repo scope (PAT method only)

Cause: The one-time code may have expired (codes are valid for approximately 15 minutes) or was entered incorrectly. Solution: Return to Settings in CrewDeck and click Sign in with GitHub again to generate a new code Visit github.com/login/device promptly and enter the new code If the problem persists, fall back to Personal Access Token authentication
documents.s: GitHub Device Flow code not accepted

documents.t: Cause: Any of the following: The attachment was never saved (Save Secrets was not clicked), or it was removed The secret was deleted, or its key was renamed while the server's Headers or Config still contain a ${KEY} reference you typed with the old name, so that reference is left unresolved The server is not enabled for the project the task runs in The Server Type was changed between stdio and http, and the attachment was not re-saved for the new type The session started before the secret was attached or its value was replaced The provider expects a different header or variable name, or a Bearer prefix The operating system's credential store was unavailable, so the attachment was skipped with a warning Solution: Open Settings › AI & Tools › MCP Servers, click Edit on the server and check that the secret is listed under Secrets. If not, attach it and click Save Secrets Check that the secret still exists under Secrets with the expected key Check that the server is enabled for the project If you changed the Server Type, save it, reopen the server, correct the flagged attachment and click Save Secrets Compare the target name with your provider's documentation. For a Bearer scheme, type Authorization: Bearer ${YOUR_KEY} in the server's Headers field Restart the session, or start a new run, so the current values are picked up See Custom Secrets for MCP Servers for details.
documents.s: MCP server fails to authenticate after attaching a secret

documents.t: Cause: The repository may not contain agent definitions, or they weren't discovered. Solution: Verify the repo has a .claude/agents/ directory with agent files Go to Repos tab and click Sync next to the repository Check the Agents tab to see discovered agents
documents.s: Agent not found in connected repos

documents.t: Cause: The process may be waiting for input or stuck. Solution: Try clicking in the terminal and pressing Enter If truly stuck, click the Terminate button Retry the task after investigating the error

Cause: The execution may have failed or been interrupted. Solution: Check the terminal output for errors If the process is no longer running, manually drag the task back to "To Do" Address any errors shown in the terminal before retrying

Cause: Git credentials or token may have insufficient permissions. Solution: Verify your GitHub token has the repo scope Ensure you have access to the repository on GitHub Try disconnecting and reconnecting the repository
documents.s: Clone failed or repository access denied

documents.t: Cause: Claude Code CLI may not be installed or not in PATH. Solution: Run npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code Verify installation with claude --version Restart CrewDeck after installing
documents.s: Command execution fails with "command not found"

documents.t: Cause: GitHub CLI (gh) may not be authenticated. Solution: Open a terminal and run gh auth login Follow the prompts to authenticate with GitHub Retry the task

Cause: A worktree with the same name may already exist. Solution: Check if the worktree directory exists in ~/Library/Application Support/crewdeck/worktrees/ Manually delete orphaned worktrees if needed Retry the task
Cause: No repositories are connected to the project. Solution: Navigate to the Crew → Repos tab Connect at least one GitHub repository The three tabs appear under Crew once a repository is connected
documents.s: Agents, Commands or Skills tab not visible

documents.t: Cause: Claude CLI error, network issues, or timeout during AI generation. Solution: Check that Claude Code CLI is installed (claude --version) Verify your network connection Try again with a simpler or more specific description Check the terminal output for specific error messages

Cause: Git or GitHub permission issues preventing branch creation or commits. Solution: Verify your GitHub token has write permissions to the repository Ensure the repository is not read-only or archived Check if branch protection rules are blocking the operation Try disconnecting and reconnecting the repository

Cause: Unable to create a branch or PR for the removal operation. Solution: Verify GitHub is connected in Settings Check your token has push access to the repository Ensure no branch with the same name already exists Review the terminal output for specific errors

Cause: The AI coding tool is not installed or not in your PATH. Solution: Go to Settings > AI Coding Tools Click Detect Tools to scan for installed tools If your tool shows as unavailable: Install the tool following its documentation Ensure the CLI command is in your system PATH Restart CrewDeck and detect tools again For specific tools: Claude Code: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code Cursor: Install from cursor.sh Gemini CLI: Install from Google's documentation GitHub Copilot: Install GitHub CLI with gh extension install github/gh-copilot

Cause: The repository has modified files that haven't been committed. Solution: Open a terminal in the repository directory Run git status to see what files are modified Either: Commit the changes: git add . && git commit -m "your message" Or stash them: git stash Return to CrewDeck and click Refresh again

Cause: The session may have terminated or the reconnection failed. Solution: Check if the original task is still running (look for the task in "In Progress") If the session appears disconnected, try: Clicking on the task card to view its terminal Restarting the task if needed Check the terminal output for any error messages
documents.s: Terminal sessions not reconnecting after refresh

documents.t: Cause: You've reached the maximum concurrent session limit. Solution: Close or terminate sessions you no longer need Wait for running tasks to complete To increase the limit: Go to Settings > Terminal Adjust Max Concurrent Sessions (default: 10, max: 20) Note: Running many sessions simultaneously increases memory usage. Monitor your system resources if you frequently run 15+ sessions.

Cause: No AI agents are currently running, or only interactive terminal sessions are open. Solution: The agent indicator only shows when AI agents (like build-feature, code-reviewer) are running Interactive terminal sessions are not counted as agents Start a task with an assigned agent to see the indicator The indicator automatically appears/disappears as agents start and complete

Cause: Ollama is not running or required models are not installed. Solution: Ensure Ollama is installed from https://ollama.ai Start Ollama: ollama serve Install required models: ollama pull mistral:7b ollama pull nomic-embed-text Check LLM status indicator in chat panel (should be green) Click "Index Docs" to index documentation before chatting

Cause: Documentation has not been indexed or is not in the correct location. Solution: Ensure your primary repository has a docs/ folder with .md files Navigate to the project (chat is project-scoped) Click Index Docs in the chat panel Wait for indexing to complete Try your question again

Cause: Claude CLI not available or repository not properly configured. Solution: Verify Claude CLI is installed: claude --version Ensure you have at least 2 agents selected Check that agents exist in your project Verify repository has local path configured Check terminal output for specific error messages

Cause: No active suggestions have been generated or all have been dismissed. Solution: Suggestions are currently generated manually (future enhancement) Dismissed suggestions are filtered out automatically The panel automatically hides when no active suggestions exist

Cause: Variables may not be using correct syntax or values not provided. Solution: Ensure variables use double curly braces: {{variable_name}} Variable names must be alphanumeric with underscores/dashes only Provide values for all variables when creating task from template Check template preview to verify interpolation

Cause: Chain may have stopped on error (default behavior). Solution: Check terminal output for failed step Review "Continue on Error" setting: Off (default): Stops at first failed step On: Continues executing remaining steps Fix the failing command or enable continue-on-error if appropriate
documents.s: Command chain not executing in order

documents.t: Cause: Git configuration, permissions, or Claude CLI issues. Solution: Verify Claude CLI is installed and authenticated Check GitHub token has push permissions Ensure repository is not in detached HEAD state Check terminal output for specific git errors Verify no uncommitted changes in repository

Cause: Repository permissions or git issues. Solution: Verify GitHub token has write permissions to repository Ensure repository is not read-only or archived Check if branch protection rules are blocking the operation Review the error message in the agent detail modal For PR-based installs, check that PR was created and merge it

Cause: Outcomes may not be automatically recorded yet. Solution: Outcomes are currently recorded manually when tasks complete Future enhancement will include automatic recording Check if task has been moved to "Done" status Verify database schema is up to date

Cause: Sidebar may be collapsed or operation failed. Solution: Expand the sidebar to see reorder controls Hover over project to reveal up/down buttons First project cannot move up Last project cannot move down Changes should persist immediately - refresh if needed

Cause: Fewer than 2 agents are assigned to the task. Solution: The Agent Execution Mode toggle only appears when 2 or more agents are assigned Add additional agents to the task to see the toggle Single-agent tasks always use the standard execution flow

Cause: The first selected agent is not an orchestrator type. Solution: For best results with swarm mode, select an orchestrator agent (e.g., feature-orchestrator, bugfix-orchestrator) as the first agent If no orchestrator is detected, CrewDeck defaults to feature-orchestrator Ensure the default orchestrator exists in your connected repository

Cause: No task outcomes have been recorded yet, or there is a data loading error. Solution: Analytics require completed tasks with recorded outcomes Complete tasks and provide ratings to populate analytics data If an error message appears, click the Retry button Try a different date range to check if data exists for other periods

Cause: No agent performance data has been recorded. Solution: Agent performance data is populated when tasks complete with outcomes Run tasks with assigned agents and allow them to complete Verify that agents are discovered in your project's Agents tab Check date range filters -- try "All Time" to see all available data

Cause: Rankings have not been calculated yet, or agents have insufficient data. Solution: Rankings are calculated automatically when task outcomes are recorded Agents need at least one completed task to receive a ranking Low-confidence rankings (fewer than 10 tasks) are shown with dashed borders Navigate to the Agent Performance page to verify rankings exist

Cause: In versions prior to v0.15.0, a background color mismatch caused a visible black border to appear around the terminal area. Solution: This is resolved in v0.15.0. Update to the latest version. If the border still appears after updating, try closing and reopening the terminal panel.
documents.s: Black border visible around terminal content

documents.t: Cause: The pause button only appears for running sessions. Solution: Verify the terminal session is actively running (animated spinner visible) The pause button appears only in the tab header of running sessions Completed or failed sessions cannot be paused If the button is unresponsive, try clicking directly on the pause icon

Cause: CPU or memory usage has reached critical levels. Solution: Close or terminate terminal sessions you no longer need Wait for running tasks to complete Check the error message for specific resource usage percentages The message suggests how many sessions to close to free resources System health refreshes every 30 seconds -- wait and retry

Cause: GitHub is not connected, or there are permission issues. Solution: Verify GitHub is connected in Settings Ensure your token has the repo scope for repository creation Check that the repository name follows GitHub naming rules (no spaces, cannot start with a period) If the name already exists on your account, choose a different name
documents.s: Create New Repo button not working

documents.t: Cause: Only one repository is connected to the project. Solution: Primary/Context badges only appear when multiple repositories are connected Connect a second repository to see the badge distinction The first connected repository is automatically set as primary

Cause: The task may not be in the "Document" column. Solution: The Document Wizard only activates for tasks in the "Document" column Ensure the task has been moved to "Document" status Tasks in other columns use the standard terminal execution flow Check that the task has a PR link (documentation workflows require a prior PR)

Cause: The task may already be in "Done" status or has been released. Solution: The "Mark as Failed" action is available on active task cards on the Kanban board Tasks already in "Done" or released status cannot be marked as failed Look for the warning icon on the task card, or open the task detail view
documents.s: Mark as Failed option not visible

documents.t: Cause: Telemetry is disabled by default. Solution: Go to Settings > Telemetry Enable the master telemetry toggle Enable specific categories you want to track Telemetry events are batched and flushed every 30 seconds

Cause: Feedback prompts are disabled or the workflow category is turned off. Solution: Go to Settings > Feedback Enable the Prompts Enabled toggle Ensure the specific workflow category is enabled (e.g., "Task Completion") Prompts appear once per workflow completion -- they do not repeat for the same event

Cause: The worktree may have already been removed, or cleanup encountered an error. Solution: Worktree cleanup is non-blocking -- it does not affect your rating Check if the worktree folder still exists: ls ~/Library/Application\ Support/crewdeck/worktrees/ Manually delete orphaned worktree folders if needed Run git worktree prune in the source repository to clean stale references
documents.s: Worktree not cleaned up after rating

documents.t: Cause: The attachment may not have been saved correctly, or the file was moved. Solution: Verify the file was uploaded by opening the task detail view Attachments are stored in CrewDeck's local data directory If the original file was deleted from disk, the attachment link may be broken Re-attach the file if needed

Cause: Update server may be unreachable, or the app was installed in a read-only location. Solution: Ensure you have an internet connection Restart the application to trigger an update check Verify the application was installed in a writable location Check for error notifications regarding update failures
Version 0.19.0 introduces JIRA integration, remote device pairing, session resume, and several improvements to the task execution pipeline.
Connect your Atlassian JIRA Cloud instance to import issues as CrewDeck tasks and sync status changes back to JIRA. See Importing JIRA Issues as Tasks for setup instructions.

Pair a remote device (phone, tablet, or secondary computer) with your CrewDeck instance using QR code scanning. Once paired, the remote device can monitor task progress and receive notifications. Pairing uses TLS-encrypted JWT authentication. How to Pair Go to Settings > Remote Devices Click Generate Pairing Code Scan the QR code with the CrewDeck companion app on your device The device appears in the paired devices list
Resume specific previous Claude CLI sessions by ID from the terminal panel. See Session Resume for details.
Agents can now emit a <TASK_COMPLETED/> sentinel token to signal task completion explicitly, improving detection reliability beyond process exit alone.

In sequential execution mode, agents can pass structured handoff files to the next agent in the chain, enabling explicit context transfer. Each handoff includes a summary, file list, and suggested next steps.
Before agent execution, CrewDeck automatically runs npm install in any mcp-servers/ subdirectories in the worktree, ensuring MCP tool dependencies are available.
Configure a SonarCloud/SonarQube API key in Settings that is securely injected into agent sessions. See Sonar API Key in the Settings documentation.

Credential notification auto-dismiss: Duplicate credential access notifications are suppressed with a 5-second auto-dismiss timer excludeRules frontmatter: Agent YAML files now support excludeRules frontmatter for excluding specific rules during execution Relative paths hook: A PreToolUse hook automatically converts absolute paths to relative paths in agent tool calls data-testid attributes: Key UI elements now include data-testid attributes for E2E test automation E2E test fixtures: Playwright-based test infrastructure with per-test database isolation CREWDECK_DB_PATH environment variable: Override the database path for test isolation and custom deployments

Fixed database transaction error handling in concurrent operations Fixed net::ERR_FAILED handling for network request failures Improved sentinel detection reliability in terminal output Fixed JIRA API migration for updated Atlassian endpoints Resolved terminal rendering artifacts during high-output sessions Fixed jobs failing when resuming from system sleep Corrected sentinel prompt passing to agent execution context Eliminated developer console errors from CSP blob worker violations Fixed session restart failure when previous session state was corrupted
Version 0.24.0 introduces autonomy for automatic task progression, LLM-enhanced transcript downloads, a reorganized Settings page, and notification reliability fixes.

Autonomy is a premium feature that automatically advances tasks through Kanban columns after successful execution. When enabled, completing a task in one stage (e.g., In Progress) automatically commits and pushes the working branch, moves the task to the next column (e.g., In Review), and begins execution of the next stage -- all without requiring the user to click "Run." In v0.25.0, autonomy was extended to automatically start the next todo task in the project after the current task reaches the Done stage, enabling fully autonomous task chaining across an entire project backlog. How to Enable Go to Settings > AI & Tools Enable Turbo Mode (required prerequisite) Toggle Autonomy on Stage Progression Completed Stage Next Stage Auto-Executes? In Progress In Review Yes In Review Document Yes Document Done No (terminal stage) Done Next Todo Task Yes (v0.25.0) Safety Mechanisms Only triggers on successful completion -- failures, manual cancellations, and sleep-related exits are excluded Deduplication guard prevents duplicate auto-executions for the same task All existing gates (health checks, agent permissions, capacity queuing) are respected Turning off Turbo Mode automatically disables Autonomy
The Save Transcript feature now produces richer output when Ollama is available. See Download Formatted Markdown Transcript for details.

The Settings page has been reorganized from a single scrollable view into six tabbed groups: Integrations, Notifications, Sandbox & Terminal, Security, AI & Tools, and Data & Privacy. Tabs are URL-synced for deep-linking and browser navigation. See Settings Page for the full layout.

Fixed false idle notifications on active task-execution sessions -- the notification service now correctly tracks output activity during all execution phases Fixed false question notifications caused by Claude's internal reasoning output (e.g., "Is this correct? Let me verify...") triggering question detection Stale question lines in the sliding window no longer re-trigger detection after cooldown expiry

Version 0.25.0 adds allowed directories to the sandbox configuration, extends autonomy to chain across tasks, moves settings tabs to the right side, and fixes several terminal and release process issues.

The sandbox security policy now includes an Allowed Directories field, letting you whitelist additional filesystem paths that Claude Code agents can access beyond the default worktree path. Configure this in Settings > Sandbox & Terminal > Terminal Sandbox. The worktree path is always auto-included and deduplicated. See Sandbox Security Policy Configuration for details.

Autonomy now chains across tasks: when a task reaches the Done stage, the system automatically finds and starts the next todo task in the same project (ordered by Kanban position). This enables fully autonomous processing of an entire project backlog. A 2-second delay between tasks allows post-completion actions to finish. See Autonomy (Premium) for the full stage progression table.

Settings page tab navigation has been moved from the left side to the right side of the screen. The settings content is now positioned directly adjacent to the app sidebar for a more natural reading flow.

The Save Transcript feature now captures only the interactive agent execution phase of a session, filtering out preparation noise (worktree creation, branch syncing, prompt refinement). This applies to Build, Review, and Document workflows. Raw log exports (Save Output) continue to include the full session output.

Release process completion: Fixed the release wizard hanging indefinitely after workflow completion. The release:complete event is now emitted before the session sender is unregistered, ensuring the completion signal reaches the renderer. Terminal rendering artifacts on tab switch: Fixed garbled terminal output when switching between tabs by adding missing post-render refresh and texture atlas reset calls for WebGL sessions.

Version 0.27.0 introduces centralized backlog management, execution status indicators, a unified task queue, PR discovery and monitoring, dynamic PTY pool sizing, PTY process tree monitoring, and a Claude Code hook for GitHub MCP redirection.

The Backlog panel provides a centralized queue for task ideas and planned work items. Backlog items can be created directly, enriched with AI-generated context, and pulled into project Kanban boards when ready. The panel now organizes items into collapsible epic-grouped sections with intelligent readiness indicators and cost estimation. Backlog Item Organization & Filtering (v0.71.0)​ Epic-grouped sections: Backlog items are now organized into collapsible sections grouped by epic. Each section header displays the item count, a readiness-weighted progress bar showing documentation, specification, and dependency readiness, and the aggregated cost estimate for all items in the section. Advanced filtering: Use the backlog toolbar to filter items by title search, repository, priority, category, or by readiness status. The "Ready only" toggle shows only items with all three readiness segments complete. All filters work together to dynamically update epic sections and cost rollups. Multi-select bulk actions: Select multiple backlog items using per-row checkboxes. Once items are selected, a bulk action bar appears with two options: Dispatch to Agent: Opens a one-screen confirmation summary listing the resolved agent for each dispatchable item and skip reasons for any items that cannot be dispatched. Confirm to create task execution sessions. Promote to Board: Immediately promotes selected items to the project Kanban board without confirmation. Cost Estimation (v0.71.0)​ Degraded cost-estimator banner: When cost estimates are unavailable, cached, or degraded (due to insufficient calibration data), a banner appears at the top of the backlog. The banner indicates the current state and provides a Retry button to refresh the estimates. Per-item cost display: Each backlog item shows an estimated dollar cost, helping prioritize work based on implementation effort. Per-epic cost rollup: Epic section headers sum the estimated costs of all items in that section, providing quick visibility into epic-level effort investment. Backlog Item Detail Panel (v0.71.0)​ Item readiness status: Backlog items display per-item readiness status with three color-coded segments: docs ready, specs ready, and dependencies ready. A summary badge shows overall readiness at a glance. Generate Tasks: The detail panel includes a Generate Tasks button that creates a breakdown of subtasks from the backlog item requirements, powered by AI task decomposition.

Task cards on the Kanban board now display real-time execution sub-state indicators. When a task is running, the card shows the current execution phase (e.g., cloning, building, testing, reviewing) with animated status badges. This provides at-a-glance visibility into what each AI agent is actively doing.

Stage execution and new task starts are now routed through a single TaskQueueService. The queue dashboard panel (accessible from the Kanban board header) shows pending and active queue entries with type badges and dispatch countdown timers. This ensures orderly task processing and prevents race conditions when multiple tasks complete simultaneously.

A new PR discovery service automatically finds eligible open pull requests across connected repositories. This powers the upcoming PR auto-fix background agent and provides the foundation for automated PR monitoring workflows.

Database schema additions support PR watch lists and fix attempt tracking. Projects can now register PRs for monitoring, and the system records fix attempts with status and metadata for audit purposes.

The PTY process pool now dynamically adjusts its size based on the autonomy concurrency setting. When autonomy processes multiple tasks in parallel, the pool pre-warms additional PTY processes to maintain instant session creation. Pool size scales proportionally and respects system resource constraints.

A new process tree monitor detects stuck subprocesses in PTY sessions. When a child process (e.g., a hung git operation) exceeds configurable time thresholds, the monitor flags the session and can optionally terminate the stuck process. This prevents zombie sessions from consuming resources indefinitely.

A new PreToolUse hook intercepts gh CLI commands and curl/wget calls targeting api.github.com, blocking direct execution and guiding Claude to use the GitHub MCP tools (mcp__github__*) instead. This ensures all GitHub operations go through the MCP layer for consistent auditing and rate limiting.
documents.s: Claude Code Hook for GitHub MCP

documents.t: The Create Debate modal now includes a Purpose dropdown, allowing users to categorize debates (e.g., architecture decision, implementation review, trade-off analysis). This improves debate organization and filtering in the Decision Journal.

An explicit task state machine service enforces valid state transitions for tasks. Invalid transitions (e.g., moving a blocked task to in-progress) are rejected with clear error messages. This replaces ad-hoc status checks scattered across multiple services.

Missing decomposition_feedback table: Fixed scoring submission failures caused by the decomposition_feedback table not being created during migration. Diagnostic mode toggle stuck: Fixed the diagnostic mode toggle in setup remaining stuck in the off state after enabling. Missing agent auto-assignment: Fixed task decomposition not auto-assigning agents to decomposed sub-tasks when a matching agent exists in the repository. Dependency PR status check: Task modals now re-check dependency PR merge status when opened, preventing stale dependency indicators.

If you encounter issues not covered in this guide: Check the terminal output for specific error messages For chat issues, check Ollama logs: ollama logs For marketplace issues, review the PR created on GitHub Report issues at github.com/cloudnnj/crewdeck-issues
Create complex multi-agent workflows with dependency relationships using Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) execution mode.

Complex Dependencies: When one agent's output feeds directly into another agent's input Conditional Branching: When you want certain agents to run only after others complete Optimal Parallelization: The system automatically parallelizes agents with no dependencies on each other Large Teams: Provides clearer visibility into multi-agent execution order for teams with 5+ agents

Create or edit a task with multiple agents In the execution mode selector, choose "DAG (Dependency graph)" The visual graph builder appears with all agents as nodes Drag arrows between agents to define dependencies (Agent A → Agent B means A must complete before B starts) Save the task with your graph configuration

Add Dependencies: Click and drag from one agent to another to create a dependency arrow Remove Dependencies: Click on an arrow to delete it Validate Graph: The system automatically detects and prevents circular dependencies Reset Graph: Clear all dependencies and start fresh Visual Feedback: Completed agents appear highlighted; agents ready to run are shown in blue

Agents with no dependencies start immediately Agents wait for all their dependencies to complete before starting Multiple agents run in parallel when their dependencies allow If any agent fails, dependent agents are blocked and marked as "waiting"
Task execution now accurately tracks time from job inception through completion, including all pre-Claude stages.
documents.s: Elapsed Time Accuracy for Task Execution (v0.37.0)

documents.t: Complete Duration: Elapsed time now includes worktree setup, dependency installation, MCP configuration, and prompt refinement — not just Claude's execution time Accurate Completion: When a task finishes (success or failure), the elapsed time display freezes at the final value instead of continuing to tick Real Job Duration: The "Elapsed" KPI in the Activity Panel now represents the true wall-clock time from task start to finish

The Activity Panel shows: While Running: MM:SS that updates every second (total elapsed time including pre-Claude stages) After Completion: Frozen MM:SS value equal to total job duration Multiple Concurrent Tasks: Each task's timer is independent; pausing one does not affect others
The elapsed time accuracy applies to all SDK-based execution stages: Normal task execution PR review workflows Documentation generation
Improved filtering capabilities help organize and manage large numbers of tasks and hooks across multiple projects.

The task list now supports: Project Scope: View tasks for a specific project Status Filter: Show tasks by status (todo, in_progress, done, in_review, document) Assignment: Filter by assigned agent Date Range: View tasks created or updated in a specific time period Keyword Search: Search in task titles and descriptions

The hooks management interface provides: Hook Type: Filter by event type (on task start, on completion, on failure, etc.) Project Scope: View hooks for specific projects Active/Inactive: Show only enabled or disabled hooks Trigger Search: Find hooks by their trigger conditions

documents.t: Hover over a task in the list to see the full subject line (if it exceeds the visible area) The preview appears in a tooltip showing the complete task description Links from task descriptions are visible in the preview Use this to quickly identify duplicate or related tasks before opening them

Quick Navigation: Jump directly from a task's activity card to its related PR PR Status Visibility: See if the PR is still in draft, open for review, or merged Unified View: Track task execution and PR progress from a single dashboard Multiple Repos: Links work across all connected repositories

Version 0.10.0 is a major performance and infrastructure release that dramatically improves terminal rendering speed, system resource management, and task workflow capabilities. This release introduces GPU-accelerated terminal rendering via WebGL, RAF-based output batching for smooth 60 FPS output, intelligent viewport-aware session prioritization, comprehensive performance instrumentation dashboards, and event sourcing architecture for full state change auditing. The release also adds critical workflow enhancements including task failure logging, automatic worktree cleanup, bidirectional GitHub Issue synchronization, context-driven task development, and AI-generated daily activity summaries. Additionally, the release includes 10 bug fixes addressing terminal display issues, dashboard analytics accuracy, and configuration defaults.

RAF-Based Terminal Output Batching — requestAnimationFrame-based output batching with visibility detection for hidden tabs, reducing CPU usage during background terminal operation Viewport-Aware Session Prioritization — Background terminals buffer aggressively (150ms intervals) while visible terminals get immediate processing (16ms/60 FPS) for optimal responsiveness Pause/Resume Output Control — Manual pause/resume for terminal sessions with buffering capability, enforcing 500KB buffer limits to prevent memory growth Performance Instrumentation Dashboard — Real-time metrics for PTY latency, IPC latency, event loop lag (50ms threshold), and render time with historical charting System Health Monitoring — CPU/memory health gate preventing session creation when system is overloaded (95% CPU or critical memory pressure) WebGL Terminal Renderer — GPU-accelerated terminal rendering using @xterm/addon-webgl with automatic fallback to Canvas on context loss Event Loop Lag Reduction — Reduced main process event loop lag below 50ms threshold via async file I/O, deferred event sourcing writes, and timer jitter Event Sourcing Architecture — Immutable event log capturing all state changes in state_events table with 180-day retention and 50K event limit

Task Failure Logging — Mark tasks as failed from kanban board with optional task recreation, tracking failures in outcome system for analytics Worktree Cleanup on Task Rating — Automatic worktree folder removal after task completion rating via git worktree remove to reclaim disk space Context-Driven Task Development — Copy context repo files (docs, DEPARTMENTS.md) into worktree .crewdeck-context/ folder for agent access without prompt size limits

Automatic PR Comments — Structured GitHub PR comments summarizing agent activity, execution phases, key decisions, command chain progress, and timing data on task completion Bidirectional GitHub Issue Synchronization — Two-way sync between CrewDeck tasks and GitHub Issues with status mapping (todo ↔ crewdeck:todo label), 60-second polling for merge detection, and conflict resolution

This release ships five CrewDeck MCP servers inside the app instead of fetching them from GitHub Packages with npx. The knowledge-graph and intelligence servers are available on Pro plans. End users no longer need a GitHub Packages token, and the setting that held one is hidden in packaged builds. Two fixes correct GitHub auth status reporting and stop release cleanup from deleting worktrees that tasks are still using. Generalizes the bundled MCP server launch so every CrewDeck server can start from the app bundle, not only crewdeck-data. Packages the crewdeck-git-ops MCP server inside the app. Replaces CrewDeck-owned MCP registry rows with a launch from the app bundle when the flag is on. Custom rows are left unchanged. Retires the end-user GitHub Packages token: provisioning no longer writes an .npmrc for it, and the setting is hidden in packaged builds. GitHub auth status now reports a clear state on every failure path instead of rejecting the IPC call or reporting a misleading negative result. Release cleanup no longer deletes worktrees for tasks that are still refining their prompts, because those worktrees have no manifest yet.

Version 0.11.0 is a major architecture and reliability release focused on codebase quality, developer experience, and PTY session stability. This release introduces a decomposed IPC handler architecture replacing the monolithic handlers.ts, standardized error handling with ServiceResult<T>, centralized configuration constants, and an ACK-based worker termination protocol. Key user-facing additions include a searchable decision journal for multi-agent debates, comprehensive JSON/YAML data export/import, automatic GitHub Issue closing on task completion, debate UI improvements (timer, background mode, animated output), and collaboration telemetry instrumentation. The release also delivers 10 critical bug fixes addressing PTY memory leaks, session management issues, and terminal behavior.

Version 0.12.0 is a major feature and intelligence release focused on task management intelligence, terminal performance, and security hardening. This release introduces a comprehensive task dependency system with DAG validation, AI-powered natural language task creation, auto-task decomposition from epics, intelligent agent selection with confidence scoring, cross-task learning from historical patterns, and failure pattern detection with intelligent retry suggestions. Terminal performance receives significant upgrades including Unix domain socket IPC bypass, binary data transfer, predictive pre-buffering, and proactive memory compaction. Security improvements include a new permission hook system replacing --dangerously-skip-permissions, security audit logging with SQLite event store, and corporate proxy support. The release also adds Team execution mode, pause/resume task execution, git-based team data sharing, and alternative branching strategy support.

Task Dependency System (PR #503) — DAG-validated task dependencies with 3 relationship types (blocks, requires, relates to), cycle detection, and status gating to enforce execution order Task Dependency Types & Metadata (PR #504) — Enhanced dependency edges with type classification, metadata columns, and DAG query support for complex workflows Auto-Task Decomposition (PR #604) — Break down large epics into smaller subtasks using Claude AI, with automatic inter-subtask dependency wiring, parent-child blocking, and quality feedback loop Natural Language Task Creation (PR #577) — AI-powered extraction of structured task fields (title, description, priority, agents) from free-form natural language descriptions with confidence scoring Intelligent Agent Selection (PR #558) — Confidence-scored agent recommendations using hybrid scoring: 60% composite ranking + 40% semantic similarity + user override boost with 30-day decay Cross-Task Learning Service (PR #600) — Historical pattern injection service that learns from past task executions to improve future suggestions, with timer-safe cleanup and security-hardened inputs Failure Pattern Detection (PR #609) — Automatic analysis of terminal output and execution data to detect failure patterns (timeout, missing dependency, agent mismatch, resource exhaustion, permission errors) with intelligent recovery strategy suggestions Task Intelligence & Embeddings (PR #577) — Semantic search using Voyage AI embeddings (voyage-3-lite) with TF-IDF keyword fallback, circuit breaker protection, and budget tracking

Team Execution Mode (PR #563) — New agent execution mode enabling team-based parallel execution alongside existing sequential and swarm modes Pause/Resume Task Execution (PR #548) — Pause and resume running tasks, allowing agents to be temporarily halted and restarted without losing context Git-Based Team Data Sharing (PR #547) — Share releases and activity summaries across team members via git commits, enabling collaborative project management Export-to-PR Workflow (PR #558) — Export department data and team exports via git worktree-based pull requests for review-gated data sharing Command-Orchestrated Agent Read-Only (PR #576) — Agents assigned through command orchestration are now read-only in task modals, preventing accidental modification Task Execution Guard (PR #547) — Prevent execution of tasks without agents or command assigned, avoiding empty terminal sessions

Unix Domain Socket IPC Bypass (PR #596) — Terminal data bypass using Unix domain sockets for lower-latency communication between PTY workers and renderer Binary Data Transfer (PR #564) — Switch terminal data transfer from string encoding to Uint8Array binary format, reducing serialization overhead Predictive Pre-Buffering (PR #600) — Pre-buffer terminal data for tab switches, providing instant content display when switching between terminal sessions Proactive Memory Compaction (PR #576) — Automatic memory compaction for idle terminal sessions, reclaiming V8 heap space during inactivity Terminal Performance Profiling (PR #603) — Infrastructure for profiling terminal pipeline performance with end-to-end latency tracking V8 GC Tuning (PR #621) — Per-process V8 garbage collection tuning flags (--max-old-space-size, --optimize-for-size) optimized for terminal workloads Cap Per-Frame Terminal Writes (PR #559) — Limit terminal write operations per animation frame to prevent UI jank during high-volume output

Permission Hook System (PR #622) — Replace --dangerously-skip-permissions flag with @abdo-el-mobayad/claude-code-fast-permission-hook three-tier system: fast approve (safe ops), fast deny (dangerous ops), LLM analysis (ambiguous cases) Security Audit Logging (PR #623) — SQLite event store for security audit logging, tracking all security-relevant events with structured metadata Corporate Proxy Support (PR #630) — SSL/TLS certificate environment variables passed to PTY processes and Electron net.fetch for GitHub API calls, enabling use behind corporate proxies Tool Invocation Telemetry (PR #558) — Track tool invocations with skip-permissions policy telemetry for security analytics App Refresh Protection (PR #591) — Block browser refresh when active terminal sessions exist, preventing accidental process termination Sleep Prevention Investigation (PR #594) — Caffeinate integration investigation for preventing system sleep during long-running tasks

Alternative Branching Strategies (PR #623) — Per-project branching strategy configuration supporting trunk-based, GitFlow, and custom branch patterns Release Workflow Improvements (PR #622) — Abort release when no changes committed, cleanup stale release worktrees, version validation Stale Worktree Cleanup During Release (PR #564) — Release workflow now cleans up all stale task worktrees belonging to included tasks

Version 0.13.0 is a security-focused release delivering comprehensive hardening across every layer of the application. This release introduces BrowserWindow sandbox mode with main-process IPC migration, Zod-based input validation on all IPC channels, prompt injection detection with an LLM input firewall, PBKDF2 key derivation for secure storage, Content Security Policy hardening, command risk classification, and automated dependency vulnerability scanning in CI. Version 0.14.0 delivers a comprehensive framework modernization, a full telemetry pipeline, and continued security and terminal hardening. On the framework side, this release upgrades Electron 38 to 40 (with electron-vite 3 to 5), migrates react-router-dom 6 to 7 across 17+ files, upgrades @xterm/xterm 5 to 6, @dnd-kit/sortable 8 to 10, @octokit/rest 20 to 22, ESLint 9 to 10, and @testing-library/react 14 to 16. Security hardening continues with dual blocklist/allowlist executable control, parameterized spawn replacing shell string concatenation, Chromium renderer sandbox restoration via CJS preload conversion, IPC sender frame validation, removal of raw GitHub token exposure from the renderer, Electron safeStorage credential fallback, production CSP hardening, and sandbox security policy configuration. A new opt-in telemetry pipeline forwards anonymized usage data to a remote API with SHA-256 hashed user IDs, batched delivery with exponential backoff, sampling rate configuration, and a transparent first-run opt-in prompt. Terminal improvements include save-to-file output export, cursor-up-aware ring buffer storage fixing progress indicator stacking, improved padding, and interactive terminal launch reliability fixes. Task management gains per-project Kanban stage selection, configurable execution phases, two-column modal layouts for create and view/edit, shared WCAG-compliant Modal and ToggleSwitch components, and conditional epic filter visibility. The LLM stack is consolidated onto fully local Ollama with qwen3:8b and nomic-embed-text, removing the external OpenRouter dependency entirely.

Version 0.15.0 is a high-concurrency terminal performance release that fundamentally re-architects the terminal data pipeline for smooth operation at 5-6+ concurrent AI agent sessions. The release activates Multiplexer Phase 2 (consolidating per-session IPC into a single binary channel), introduces graduated three-state flow control replacing binary pause/resume, enables LZ4 compression in the worker-to-main path, adds visibility-gated writes to eliminate rendering for hidden sessions, and deploys a global RAF frame budget coordinator for jank-free multi-session rendering. Memory optimizations include dynamic PTY pool sizing, ring buffer segment compression, and faster compaction delays. On the platform side, GitHub authentication migrates from OAuth 2.0 PKCE to Device Flow (RFC 8628), Tailwind CSS upgrades from v3.4 to v4 with CSS-first configuration, the marketplace expands to support commands/skills/hooks alongside agents, and SonarCloud CI/CD quality gates are fully integrated. Four targeted bug fixes address terminal boundary rendering, release command timeouts, interactive terminal socket race conditions, and an agent dashboard infinite re-render loop.

Activate Multiplexer Phase 2 (PR #929) — Consolidated all per-session IPC into a single multiplexed binary channel via TerminalDemultiplexer.onData, disabling the legacy terminal:data IPC path and reducing IPC calls from O(N) to O(1) per flush interval Graduated Flow Control Resume (PR #928) — Replaced binary pause/resume with a three-state graduated strategy (Normal → Paused → Slow Resume → Normal) using 50ms batch intervals and adaptive backoff hysteresis, eliminating overload oscillation at 5-6 concurrent sessions WebGL Renderer Auto-Switch (PR #926) — Session-count-based WebGL promotion triggers for all terminal instances when 5+ sessions are active, eliminating Canvas/DOM main-thread blocking at high concurrency Worker-Side Priority Scheduling (PR #936) — Active (visible) terminal session PTY output is flushed synchronously before hidden sessions, which are deferred via setImmediate(), keeping the user-facing terminal responsive during background output bursts Enable LZ4 Compression in Worker (PR #937) — Activated existing LZ4 compression infrastructure in the output-batcher worker thread, compressing terminal data over 10KB before IPC transmission, reducing bandwidth 60-80% for ANSI-heavy output Dynamic PTY Pool Sizing (PR #935) — Pool target reduces to 0-1 pre-warmed PTYs when 5+ sessions are active, saving 10-30MB per idle pooled process; warmup interval suppressed when target is 0 Ring Buffer Segment Compression (PR #939) — LZ4 block compression for TerminalRingBuffer rows older than the most recent 2,000 entries in 4KB segments, achieving ~80% memory savings on historical terminal output Visibility-Gated Writes (PR #938) — Eliminated term.write() calls for non-visible terminal sessions entirely, relying on ring buffer delta replay via getRowsSince() on tab switch, reducing ~60% of renderer CPU load at 5-6 sessions Global RAF Frame Budget Coordinator (PR #942) — Replaced per-session requestAnimationFrame callbacks with a single global RAF loop using round-robin scheduling within a 12ms frame budget, with per-session error isolation Reduce Compaction Delay (PR #925) — Reduced COMPACTION_DELAY_MS from 30 seconds to 5 seconds for non-visible sessions, yielding ~40% renderer memory reduction during rapid tab-switching

GitHub OAuth Device Flow Migration (PR #930) — Migrated GitHub authentication from OAuth 2.0 PKCE (localhost callback server) to Device Flow (RFC 8628), where users enter a short code at github.com/login/device, eliminating port conflicts and simplifying the authentication UX Tailwind CSS v3.4 to v4 Migration (PR #934) — Full migration from JavaScript-based tailwind.config.js to CSS-first @theme directive model, @tailwindcss/vite plugin, and 107 deprecated outline-none → outline-hidden replacements

Version 0.16.0 is the largest release in CrewDeck history, delivering 342 features and 213 bug fixes across every layer of the application. Version 0.17.0 is a focused quality, developer tooling, and agent workflow hardening release that ships the day after v0.16.0's landmark platform modernization. The release corrects a set of high-priority bugs introduced or surfaced by the v0.16.0 upgrades — terminal output defects at narrow container widths, infinite re-render loops on the Marketplace and Templates pages, duplicate paste in interactive terminals, spurious task-completion notifications, and MCP tool permission format errors. Version 0.18.0 is the largest and most wide-ranging release in CrewDeck history, shipping approximately 350 features and 219 bug fixes across every layer of the platform. The release is organized around five major investment themes. First, AI intelligence and agent quality: thinking levels, cross-task learning, intelligent agent selection, failure pattern detection, natural language task creation, and auto-task decomposition from epics via a DAG engine bring context-aware AI behavior to the full task lifecycle. Second, terminal performance and architecture: a virtualized row-windowed renderer, WebGL GPU acceleration, worker-thread PTY management via MessagePort, LZ4 ring-buffer compression, proactive memory compaction, adaptive batch sizing, a global RAF frame budget coordinator, and visibility-gated writes deliver a dramatic reduction in memory footprint and CPU usage at high session counts. Third, task workflow depth: task dependencies with a visual DAG graph, epics, team execution mode (Claude Code agent teams), command discovery and chaining, bidirectional GitHub Issue sync, execution replay, a searchable decision journal, and a git-based team collaboration model extend the Kanban board into a full project-level workflow engine. Fourth, security hardening: replacement of --dangerously-skip-permissions with the Claude Code permission hook, command injection fixes, security audit logging infrastructure, CSP hardening, credential access controls, and npm vulnerability remediation address every outstanding security advisory. Fifth, observability and platform health: event sourcing for state changes, tool telemetry, system health monitoring with session spawn gating, performance instrumentation, error logging for AI analysis, and an Electron upgrade from 35 to 38 (Chromium 140, Node.js 22.22.0) complete the platform modernization.

When a level is selected, the service prepends the corresponding keyword instruction to the prompt before execution; the default (no selection) is unchanged Planning mode improvements — Planning mode invocations generate structured, multi-step implementation plans via an extended prompt refinement pass rather than brief summaries; the planning mode toggle is now visible and editable in both the View and Edit Task modals Cross-task learning service — CrossTaskLearningService extracts structured patterns (agent configuration, command sequence, error resolutions, key decisions) from completed tasks, stores them linked to the taskEmbeddings table, and injects the top-3 most relevant historical learnings into new task execution prompts via the existing ContextAggregationService pipeline; a feature flag and injection-tracking in taskOutcomes enable impact measurement

Intelligent agent selection with confidence scoring — Agent recommendations now use a composite 60/40 scoring formula combining AgentRankingService historical rank with TaskIntelligenceService embedding similarity, with a 15% boost for user-override signals; a three-tier fallback ensures offline scenarios still produce recommendations Natural language task creation — A "Create from Description" mode in CreateTaskModal sends a free-form English description to TaskIntelligenceService, calls the Claude CLI to extract structured fields (title, description, acceptance criteria, agent names, complexity, priority), and pre-fills the form for user review; a 5-second timeout falls back to manual entry gracefully Auto-task decomposition from epics — An "Auto-decompose" action on epic tasks uses Claude CLI with few-shot examples from CrossTaskLearningService to generate subtask breakdowns with dependency relationships and confidence scores; a review modal lets users edit, remove, or reorder before creation; created subtasks link via the task_dependencies table; quality feedback is stored for continuous improvement Intelligent dependency generation — Dependencies between AI-generated tasks are now determined by the AI at generation time based on logical relationships rather than hard-coded sequential chaining in the frontend; parallel tasks are scheduled in parallel Failure pattern detection with retry suggestions — When a task fails, the service analyzes agentTraces and taskOutcomes to classify the failure pattern (timeout, dependency error, agent-task mismatch, resource exhaustion, permission error) and surfaces actionable retry suggestions with confidence scores; successful recoveries are stored to improve future suggestions

re-attaching replays content from the ring buffer seamlessly Adaptive batch sizing — The output batcher dynamically adjusts flush intervals between 20ms (low volume) and 50ms (high volume) based on observed throughput, balancing responsiveness and IPC overhead Viewport-aware session priority — Active (visible) session PTY output is flushed synchronously; Database Browser Window — A Database entry above Settings in the sidebar opens crewdeck-db in a dedicated window. The window loads its own minimal renderer entry rather than a route in the main bundle, so it does not duplicate the application's stores and module-level IPC subscriptions. Graceful Not-Installed State — crewdeck-db is resolved from PATH and is never bundled with the app. When it is not installed, the window explains how to build it and offers a retry that works without restarting CrewDeck, so the sidebar button always opens something rather than silently doing nothing. Correct Database Selection — The TUI is spawned in the user's home directory so the CLI's own database discovery resolves to the Electron userData database the running app writes, rather than the ./data copy used by drizzle-kit in a repository checkout.

The database browser is optional. Install it with: cargo install --git https://github.com/cloudnnj/crewdeck crewdeck-cli From a repository checkout, cargo install --path crewdeck-cli works too. It requires a Rust toolchain, and opens the database strictly read-only.
