A feature release introducing packaged customer-facing documentation and scope-aware RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) for the Technical Support chat. Global chat sessions now retrieve context from shipped product documentation, while agent-scoped chat sessions gain RAG retrieval from their project's repository documentation. These changes make the AI assistant useful outside a project context and extend chat capabilities to the agent configuration interface.

Packaged Product Documentation — Customer-facing documentation (guides/, product/, releases/, and root README) is now bundled into the application binary, indexed at first launch, and available to the global "Technical Support" chat without requiring a cloned repository. Scope-Aware Chat Retrieval — The Technical Support chat retrieves from shipped product docs by default. Agent-scoped chat sessions (opened from an agent tile in project configuration) now retrieve context from the associated project's primary repository documentation. Agent Chat Documentation Citations — Assistant messages in agent-scoped chat now include source citations from retrieved repository documentation, enabling users to dive deeper into referenced topics. Index Docs Button — The "Index Docs" button is now available outside project routes, enabling product documentation indexing from anywhere. Inside a project route with an active agent session, it indexes the project's repository documentation instead. Automatic Background Indexing — Product documentation is indexed lazily on first chat use, never blocking application startup or the first message.

The doc_chunks database table has been extended with a source discriminator ('repo' | 'product') and a nullable repo_id column to support both bundled product documentation and repository-scoped documentation in a single table. A new IPC channel docs:index-product enables explicit indexing of product documentation. The docs:search channel now accepts an optional source parameter for filtering by documentation scope, maintaining backwards compatibility with existing calls.

Product documentation is stored in a compressed format within the ring buffer to minimize memory overhead. Vector search (KNN) is enabled for both product and repository documentation scopes, reducing fallback to cosine similarity over large corpora. Retrieved documentation context is capped at 12,000 characters to bound token usage and prevent prompt overflow.

Product documentation indexing requires a working embedding backend (Ollama by default). When unavailable, chat proceeds without retrieved context. Agent chat retrieves only from the project's primary repository, not secondary repositories in a multi-repo project.

After upgrading, the first global chat message will trigger a background index of product documentation. Subsequent messages will include citations from shipped docs. Existing project-scoped documentation indices remain unchanged.

A patch release that re-cuts v0.85.0. The v0.85.0 tag never produced installers: its release pipeline stopped at the test gate on infrastructure/remote-database-web/relay-client.test.ts. The application code is unchanged from v0.85.0; see the v0.85.0 release notes for the features this release ships.

Relay-client suite no longer races WebCrypto on a loaded runner. The suite's flush() helper waited a fixed 12 setImmediate rounds for the browser relay client to settle. Node resolves crypto.subtle sealing and opening on the libuv threadpool, so on the release runner a seal could outlive that budget. Three things then went wrong: a frame was not yet sent, a receipt was not yet opened, or a reply timer was armed only after the fake clock had already moved past it, which hung the test. The suite now passes the client a subtle that tracks each in-flight WebCrypto promise, and flush() drains until none remain, with a 5-second wall-clock bound so a stuck operation fails loudly. Twelve tests were affected. The fix is test-only.

This release implements ADR-0048 Track A Phase 2: workflow run and step lifecycles are now governed by transactional compare-and-set state transitions, completion guards evaluate before runs reach terminal states, and at-most-once recovery preserves paused and in-progress work. Transactional status transitions: Every workflow run and step status change is now a single SQLite transaction combining a compare-and-set UPDATE and its event row, ensuring atomicity. A stale expectation throws StaleStatusTransitionError without writing. Run-level status events: Workflow runs now emit run_status_changed events for every transition, with from/to payloads. Engine-dispatch failures retain their error event. Device-local test commands: Projects can now set a shell command per connected repository, stored locally and never synced. A new repos:update IPC channel persists the command, and the UI under Task execution shows one input per repo. Transactional event insertion: Step and run transition events are inserted within the same transaction as the status change, with sequence numbers allocated in the same idempotent loop. Completion guards: Sequential workflow runs reach completed only after branch-contains and conflict-marker guards pass. On guard failure, the run moves to paused with a recorded reason. Stalled condition: Runs that are running but have dispatched nothing for 5+ minutes now emit a run_stalled event. The sweep runs periodically, restarts safely, and checks started_at and step dispatch history. At-most-once recovery: The startup sweep now classifies runs with three outcomes: resume auto-resumeable ones (paused by the founder or a guard), fail interrupted ones (crashed mid-step), or preserve completed/failed ones. Founder-paused and guard-paused runs are no longer dropped. Task decomposition routing: Task decomposition runs now route through WorkflowRunService state transitions instead of direct writes, aligning with the single-writer rule. Retry and override guards: Runs paused by a failed completion guard can now be resumed via RETRY_GUARDS or overridden via OVERRIDE_COMPLETE lifecycle events, with a corresponding UI panel. Versioned position snapshots: In-progress workflow run positions (state, step, attempt, deadline) are persisted in a versioned, size-capped snapshot for later automatic resume. Stalled UI badge: The run history UI now shows a Stalled badge and emits the new run_stalled lifecycle event in the run timeline. Single-writer enforcement: A CI guard now fails if any file other than WorkflowRunService writes the governed workflow_runs.status or workflow_steps.status columns, with an exemption for data migrations. AgentRunSubstage derivation: The cost-ledger substage vocabulary is now defined once in a canonical tuple and derived throughout, fixing the missing mockup rank in cost-dashboard sorting. Crewdeck-data inventory: The @cloudnnj/crewdeck-data MCP server's writes are now documented and guarded: it writes six tables only (tasks, task_dependencies, epics, backlog_items, projects, system_prompts), never the governed workflow columns. Transition table tests: The full state-machine transition table is now tested with generated path-coverage tests, proving every legal edge is accepted and every missing edge is rejected.
None. The new run_status_changed event type is additive and ignored by existing consumers. The WorkflowRunStatus enum retains its six members.

This release completes the infrastructure and Lambda implementation for browser WebSocket support in the Remote Access Relay. It includes the ADR-0038 amendment that documents the browser token transport decision, the implementation of the Relay Lambda carrier logic, and the API Gateway identity source reconfiguration to enable browser connections. These changes enable Crewdeck Web to connect to the relay, pending the web application's implementation of the openRelaySocket seam.

ADR-0038 amendment: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol bearer decision — Documented how browsers send their Cognito access token through the WebSocket subprotocol since browsers cannot set the Authorization header. Added constants REMOTE_RELAY_BROWSER_WS_SUBPROTOCOL and REMOTE_RELAY_BROWSER_WS_BEARER_PREFIX to define the wire format, pinned by contract tests against the Python mirrors in the Lambda authorizer and relay. Relay Lambda carrier selection implementation — The authorizer Lambda (remote-relay-authorizer-lambda/) now extracts bearer tokens from the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header when Authorization is absent, applying the full carrier-selection matrix from ADR-0038. The relay Lambda (remote-relay-lambda/) echoes only the subprotocol name element back to browser clients, never the bearer element, as required by RFC 6455. API Gateway identity source reconfiguration — Removed the Authorization header from the relay authorizer's required identity sources, leaving only ?role= as the gateway-enforced requirement. This allows browsers to reach the authorizer without triggering a gateway-level 401. The change is idempotent and self-reconciling; re-running the deployment script confirms and repairs the configuration. Unauthorizer error mapping for credential-less connects — The authorizer raises Exception("Unauthorized") when neither carrier is present, which API Gateway maps to HTTP 401. This preserves the security baseline of rejecting credential-less attempts while moving the enforcement from the gateway to the Lambda.
None. Desktop and iOS clients continue to use the Authorization header without changes. The relay Lambdas remain compatible with existing WebSocket connections.
